{{Short description|American mathematician (born 1943)}}
'''Sheldon Mark Ross'''<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sheldon Ross |url=https://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=72362 |website=The Mathematics Genealogy Project}}</ref> (born April 30, 1943) is the Daniel J. Epstein Chair and Professor at the [[USC Viterbi School of Engineering]]. He is the author of several books in the field of probability.<ref name=INFORMS>{{Cite web|last=INFORMS|title=Ross, Sheldon M.|url=https://www.informs.org/Explore/History-of-O.R.-Excellence/Biographical-Profiles/Ross-Sheldon-M|access-date=2021-04-12|website=INFORMS|language=en-US}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Ross was born in Brooklyn.<ref name=INFORMS></ref> He received his B. S. degree in mathematics from [[Brooklyn College]] in 1963, his M.S. degrees in mathematics from [[Purdue University]] in 1964 and his Ph.D. degree in Statistics from [[Stanford University]] in 1968, studying under Gerald Lieberman and [[Cyrus Derman]]. He served as a Professor at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] from 1976 until joining the [[USC Viterbi School of Engineering]] in 2004. He serves as the Editor for several journals, among which [[Probability in the Engineering and Informational Sciences]]. In 2013 he became a fellow of the [[Institute for Operations Research and the Management Sciences]].

In 1978, he formulated what became known as [[Ross's conjecture]] in queuing theory,<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Ross|first=Sheldon M.|date=September 1978|title=Average delay in queues with non-stationary Poisson arrivals|url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-applied-probability/article/abs/average-delay-in-queues-with-nonstationary-poisson-arrivals/267BF6FF86F585CF37F1790EF43544B2|journal=Journal of Applied Probability|language=en|volume=15|issue=3|pages=602–609|doi=10.2307/3213122|jstor=3213122 |s2cid=122948002 |issn=0021-9002|url-access=subscription}}</ref> which was solved three years later by Tomasz Rolski at Poland's [[University of Wrocław|Wroclaw University]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Rolski|first=Tomasz|date=September 1981|title=Queues with non-stationary input stream: Ross's conjecture|url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/advances-in-applied-probability/article/abs/queues-with-nonstationary-input-stream-rosss-conjecture/4218BA71795B7AD9A6C213C9074364FC|journal=Advances in Applied Probability|language=en|volume=13|issue=3|pages=603–618|doi=10.2307/1426787|jstor=1426787 |s2cid=124842629 |issn=0001-8678|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

== Books ==
* Ross, S. M. (1970), ''Applied Probability Models with Optimization Applications''. Holden-Day: San Francisco, CA.
* Ross, S. M. (1972), ''Introduction to Probability Models''. [[Academic Press]]: Waltham, Mass.
* Ross, S. M. (1976), ''A First Course in Probability''. MacMillan Publishing Company: London.
* Ross, S. M. (1982), ''Stochastic Processes''. [[Wiley (publisher)|John Wiley & Sons]]: New York.
* Ross, S. M. (1983), ''Introduction to Stochastic Dynamic Programming''. Academic Press: Waltham, Mass.
* {{Cite book |last=Ross |first=Sheldon M. |title=A course in simulation |date=1990 |publisher=Macmillan ; Collier Macmillan |isbn=978-0-02-403891-3 |location=New York : London}}
* Ross, S. M. (1995), ''Introductory Statistics''. Academic Press: Waltham, Mass.
* Ross, S. M. (1996), ''Simulation''. Academic Press: Waltham, Mass.
* {{Cite book |last=Derman |first=Cyrus |title=Statistical aspects of quality control |last2=Ross |first2=Sheldon M. |date=1997 |publisher=Academic Press |isbn=978-0-12-210010-9 |series=Statistical modeling and decision science |location=San Diego}}
* {{Cite book |last=Ross |first=Sheldon M. |title=An introduction to mathematical finance: options and other topics |date=1999 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=978-0-521-77043-9 |location=Cambridge, U.K. ; New York}}
* {{Cite book |last=Ross |first=Sheldon M. |title=Topics in finite and discrete mathematics |date=2000 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=978-0-521-77259-4 |location=Cambridge ; New York}}
* {{Cite book |last=Ross |first=Sheldon M. |title=Probability models for computer science |date=2001 |publisher=Academic Press |isbn=978-0-12-598051-7 |location=San Diego, Calif.}}
* {{Cite book |last=Ross |first=Sheldon M. |title=Introduction to probability and statistics for engineers and scientists |date=2009 |publisher=Academic Press/Elsevier |isbn=978-0-12-370483-2 |edition=4th |location=Amsterdam ; Boston}}
* {{Cite book |last=Ross |first=Sheldon M. |title=A second course in probability |last2=Peköz |first2=Erol A. |date=2023 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=978-1-009-17991-1 |edition=2nd |location=Cambridge, United Kingdom ; New York, NY}}
